sources: dossier=Required behaviors bullet 2 (2026-05-16, data-platform-extensions-plan-notes, artifact-only, single-source, 'cancelling grandchildren before each row's own delete'); doc=cancel-siblings.md invariant 3 (pre-fix) sequenced the descendant walk before 'the sibling's own delete fires'; code=terminal_decision.go:121-127 deletes only when Source==OwnershipBail, otherwise calls promoteHandleState; test=auto_terminal_test.go:1103 asserts sub-claim row preserved (Promote-not-delete) past a cancel_siblings force-Abandon.
note: The dossier's own 'before delete' framing is a single uncorroborated 2026-05-16 artifact note, superseded by the later closed TerminalOutcome sum (2026-06-19, transcript) and by the 2026-05-17 Net-position bullet on promoted-row skipping, and contradicted by code and tests. Doc corrected to 'before the sibling's own terminal resolution — promotion to abandoned, or deletion under the ownership-bail source', matching claim-tree.md's already-corrected invariant.

sources: dossier=same Required-behaviors bullet 2 entry as row 184 (2026-05-16, artifact-only); doc=cancel-siblings.md invariant 3, same line as row 184; code=terminal_decision_cancel.go:91-104 resolves siblings with Source:HeldTerminal -> promoteHandleState branch in terminal_decision.go:121-127, not the OwnershipBail delete branch; test=auto_terminal_test.go:1103, 1333.
note: Duplicate confirmation of the same defect as row 184 (adjacency-check pass caught the same stale rationale). Same fix applied: invariant 3 no longer asserts a delete fires in the force-cancel frame.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 1 ('strict carries the single modifier flag cancel_siblings: true', 2026-06-19 transcript) and Corrections section ('yaml: tags were added matching every sibling struct', 2026-06-02 artifact); doc=cancel-siblings.md line 34 (pre-fix) 'strict.cancel_siblings: true' implying a nested strict: block; code=aggregation_policy.go declares kind and cancel_siblings as sibling yaml-tagged fields under error_policy, not nested under a strict: key; test=template_validator_holds_test.go:280 reports the real path as nodes[0].fan_out.error_policy.cancel_siblings.
note: Doc's own opening Definition line already correctly says the flag is declared on the fan-out parent's error policy; the line-34 shorthand contradicted it with a nonexistent nesting. Fixed to 'cancel_siblings: true on a strict error policy', consistent with the rest of the doc and with the dossier's flat-flag description.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 4 (TerminalOutcome closed sum with IsAbandon()/CauseString() helpers, 2026-06-19, transcript) and bullet 5 (sibling-cancel vs descendant-cancel distinction, 2026-06-19, transcript); doc=cancel-siblings.md Definition (pre-fix) used the undefined term 'aggregate-abandon' as the trigger; code=child_execution.go:300 fires the walk on ChildOutcome.IsAbandon(), true for OutcomeAbandon, OutcomeAbandonSiblingCancel, and OutcomeAbandonDescendantCancel; test=none directly on wording, but the closed-sum type is exercised throughout runtime tests.
note: The dossier's transcript-tier closed-sum vocabulary (any Abandon-class outcome, natural or forced) is well established and the doc's 'aggregate-abandon' term appears nowhere else in the corpus, risking misreading as the parent's post-resolution verdict. Definition reworded to 'resolves to Abandon — whether the child's own natural abandon or a forced cancel'.

sources: dossier=no cancel-siblings-specific entry on deployment topology, but the design corpus's deployment-agnostic self-containment convention (.ok-planner/CLAUDE.md: concept bodies are not a place for implementation-/deployment-specific grammar) governs concept-body wording generally; doc=cancel-siblings.md Multi-supervisor scope section (pre-fix) said 'replicas > 1 on the supervisor StatefulSet'; code=terminal_decision_cancel.go:57,130 compares HolderSupervisorID strings, a process-identity condition with no Kubernetes dependency; test=none needed, wording-only.
note: K8s-specific grammar (StatefulSet) baked a deployment artifact into a deployment-agnostic concept body, contradicted by the process-identity condition the code actually checks and by the repo's own design-doc self-containment rule. Reworded to 'more than one supervisor process running concurrently'.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 5 (sibling-cancel vs descendant-cancel are distinct mechanisms, 2026-06-19 transcript) and bullet 2 (descendant walk cancels grandchildren regardless of policy); prior ruling=claim-tree cluster rows 236/237 rewrote claim-tree.md Boundaries to own 'the recursive descendant-cancel walk (fires unconditionally whenever any claim resolves to Abandon, independent of aggregation policy or the cancel-siblings setting)' and lists cancel-siblings.md's proactive in-flight-sibling cancel under claim-tree's Does NOT own; doc=cancel-siblings.md Boundaries (pre-fix) still listed 'the recursive descendant cascade' under its own Owns, out of sync with claim-tree.md as it now stands.
note: Verified claim-tree.md already claims unconditional-descendant-walk ownership in its current Boundaries text. cancel-siblings.md Boundaries corrected: 'the recursive descendant cascade' removed from Owns, and 'the unconditional recursive descendant-cancel walk that fires on any Abandon regardless of aggregation policy (see concept:claim-tree)' added to Does NOT own, mirroring claim-tree.md's reciprocal statement. Invariant 3 (rows 184/185) was also reworded to cite concept:claim-tree for the descendant-walk mechanism rather than describing it as cancel-siblings' own.
